name: Bot and spam protection
needs: bots are signing up thousands of fake accounts
someone is testing stolen card numbers on my checkout
summary: Stopping automated traffic on forms that cost you money or reputation: signup, login, contact, checkout and anything that sends email or calls an AI. Layers work best: a hidden honeypot field, a challenge like Turnstile checked on the server, and rate limits behind both.
need_when: You see bursts of fake signups, spam messages, or failed card attempts.
A form triggers something that costs money, like an email, SMS or AI call.
skip_when: Low-traffic internal tools behind a login.

ways.title: Honeypot field and timing
ways.how: A field hidden from people that bots fill in, plus a check that the form wasn't submitted in under a second or two.
ways.tradeoff: Invisible to users. Only stops simple bots.

ways.title: Turnstile, hCaptcha or reCAPTCHA
ways.how: Add the widget, then verify the token on your server with the provider's siteverify API before doing anything. Cloudflare Turnstile tokens are single-use and expire after 300 seconds.
ways.tradeoff: Stops most automated abuse. A widget that isn't verified on the server does nothing.

ways.title: Rate limits and verification
ways.how: Limit by IP and by account, require email verification before the account can do costly things, and use your payment provider's fraud tools on checkout.
ways.tradeoff: Catches what gets past the challenge. Needs tuning so real users aren't blocked.

prompt:
Add bot protection to [signup / contact / checkout] forms.

Requirements:
- Add a honeypot field hidden with CSS (not type=hidden), with tabindex=-1 and autocomplete=off so people and password managers skip it. Reject submissions that fill it, with a generic message.
- Add Cloudflare Turnstile (or hCaptcha). On the server, verify every token with the siteverify endpoint before any other work. Reject missing, failed, expired or reused tokens.
- Keep the secret key on the server only.
- Rate-limit each form by IP and by email or account.
- New accounts must verify their email before they can [send invites / use AI / start a trial].
- Log rejected attempts with the reason (no personal data) so I can see the volume.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Submitting the form with curl and no token is rejected.
2. Reusing a token that already passed is rejected.
3. Filling the honeypot field is rejected.
4. A real user in a normal browser signs up with no extra steps beyond the widget.
5. The siteverify secret never appears in the page source.
acceptance_checks: Submitting the form with curl and no token is rejected.
Reusing a token that already passed is rejected.
Filling the honeypot field is rejected.
A real user in a normal browser signs up with no extra steps beyond the widget.
The siteverify secret never appears in the page source.
if_you_skip_it: Fake accounts, a spam-filled inbox, email sending suspended for bounces, card-testing fees and disputes, and AI bills run up by scripts.
